title: Block a crash lane: engine angled upstream across two lanes, ambulance downstream
instruction: A crashed car is stopped in the near lane of this one-way, two-lane highway (1:80 scale; traffic comes from your left, as the arrows show). Park the fire engine upstream of the car, angled 30 to 60 degrees to the lanes so it blocks both lanes, its silver pump-panel side facing the car, 50 to 125 mm (4 to 10 m) short of it. Park the ambulance downstream, straight in either lane, rear doors toward the car, 50 to 125 mm beyond it. Neither may touch the car or the other vehicle.
context: Firefighters and EMTs work highway crashes a few metres from moving traffic, and responders are struck at incident scenes every year. US traffic incident management training (the FHWA's National TIM Responder Training; NFPA 1091 covers traffic control incident management personnel) teaches the first fire apparatus to 'block': park upstream of the crash, angled across the involved lane plus one more ('lane + 1'), leaving a buffer before the work area, with the pump panel on the downstream side, where the pump operator is shielded by the apparatus. Ambulances park downstream of the crash, inside the protected area, so patients are loaded through the rear doors inside that protected space. Buffer distances differ between department SOPs; this task uses 4 to 10 m. Here a 1:80 one-way, two-lane highway stands on the table; the car crashed in the near lane, so lane + 1 is both lanes.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:80 one-way, two-lane highway runs across the table along y, from y -45.0 to +45.0 cm; traffic flows toward -y (from the robot's left to its right), so upstream is +y. Fixed, all 1 mm thick sheets lying flush side by side on the table (x ranges): (1) Grass verge: green artificial turf, x 10.0 to 15.0 cm. (2) The road, dark grey painted board: near shoulder x 15.0 to 18.6 cm; white edge line (3 mm wide) x 18.6 to 18.9 cm; lane 1, the near lane, x 18.9 to 23.1 cm; the lane line x 23.1 to 23.4 cm, white 37.5 mm dashes centred at y -37.5, -22.5, -7.5, +7.5, +22.5 and +37.5 cm with dark grey between; lane 2, the far lane, x 23.4 to 27.6 cm; yellow edge line x 27.6 to 27.9 cm; far shoulder x 27.9 to 29.5 cm. Measured to the lines' middles, lane 1 is x 18.75 to 23.25 cm and lane 2 x 23.25 to 27.75 cm (45 mm, 3.6 m, each). (3) Grass median: green turf, x 29.5 to 36.0 cm. (4) Four white painted lane arrows, 0.5 mm thick, of 5 mm wide strokes (a 40 mm shaft and two 16 mm head strokes at 45 degrees), pointing to -y, at the lane centres (x 21.0 and 25.5 cm), centred at y +41.5 and -41.5 cm. (5) The crashed car: a blue painted wooden block 22 mm (x) by 56 mm (y), 18 mm tall, with a grey-blue painted wooden cabin block 18 x 30 x 9 mm on top, centred at x 21.1 cm, y -3.0 cm and turned 10 degrees counter-clockwise seen from above, standing in lane 1 and glued to the road; it spans y -5.95 to -0.05 cm. Loose (a vehicle's middle is the middle of its overall length, on its centreline): (6) Fire engine: one rigid 80 g piece: a red painted wooden body 123 mm long, 31 mm wide and 40 mm tall, with a black windscreen 27 x 10 x 2 mm on its front face (125 mm long overall), a white light bar (24 x 6 x 3 mm) on the roof at the front, and on its left side, 15 to 30 mm forward of its middle, a silver aluminium pump panel 15 mm long, 28 mm tall and 1 mm thick, with a silver patch 15 x 10 mm on the roof edge above it; outline 125 x 32 mm. It starts in lane 2 with its middle at x 25.55 cm, y +33.0 cm, heading downstream (front toward -y, pump panel toward the median). (7) Ambulance: one rigid 50 g piece: a white painted wooden body 85 mm long, 30 mm wide and 35 mm tall, with a red stripe 4 mm tall all round 20 mm up, a dark grey rear-door panel 26 x 26 x 1 mm on its back face and a black windscreen 26 x 10 x 2 mm on its front face (88 mm long overall), and a red light bar 24 x 6 x 3 mm on the roof at the front. It starts on the near shoulder with its middle at x 17.0 cm, y -37.0 cm, front toward +y (rear doors away from the car). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the vehicles' poses at the last step, as a top photo with a tape and a protractor would read it. A vehicle's outline is its footprint seen from above (the fire engine 125 x 32 mm with its pump panel, the ambulance 88 x 30 mm; for a tilted vehicle, the shadow of its whole box). Parked: tilted 10 degrees or less, its lowest point within 3 mm of the road surface, its middle (of its overall length, on its centreline) over the road (x 15.0 to 29.5 cm), and still (moved under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s, turns counted at its corners). Distances along the road are measured in y from the car's ends: its upstream end at y -0.05 cm, its downstream end at y -5.95 cm. The trial scores 0 if either vehicle is on its side or roof (tilted more than 45 degrees), or if either vehicle's outline comes within 2 mm of the car's outline or of the other vehicle's, seen from above. Otherwise, fire engine: 0.5 if parked; its whole outline upstream of the car with a buffer (its most downstream point to the car's upstream end) of 50 to 125 mm; its long axis 30 to 60 degrees to the lanes; its outline spanning both lanes (from x 19.05 cm or less to x 27.45 cm or more: each lane's outer edge less 3 mm); and its pump-panel side facing downstream (that side's outward direction points toward -y, toward the car). 0.25 if parked, upstream with a buffer of 250 mm or less, and its outline covering at least 28 mm of lane 1's 45 mm width (x 18.75 to 23.25 cm), but not all of the 0.5 conditions. Else 0 (left in lane 2, downstream of the car, more than 250 mm back, lifted, moving or leaning). Ambulance: 0.5 if parked; its whole outline downstream of the car with a gap (the car's downstream end to its most upstream point) of 50 to 125 mm; its middle in lane 1 or 2 (x 18.75 to 27.75 cm); and its front within 15 degrees of downstream (-y), so it is straight in the lane with its rear doors toward the car. 0.25 if parked, downstream with a gap of 250 mm or less and its middle in lane 1 or 2, but not all of the 0.5 conditions. Else 0 (left on the shoulder, upstream, more than 250 mm on, lifted, moving or leaning). The score is the sum: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0, and the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Examples: the start 0; both set right 1.0; engine right, ambulance in the lane nose to the car 0.75; ambulance right and the engine square across the road (75 degrees), or angled right but with its panel toward the traffic, or straight in lane 1 behind the car (a lane block, not lane + 1) 0.75; engine right, ambulance left on the shoulder 0.5; both 0.25 cases 0.5; one 0.25 case, the other vehicle not moved 0.25; either vehicle only shoved sideways into a lane from its start (more than 250 mm from the car) 0; either vehicle pushed against the car 0. In a real trial: a tape along the lane line for the buffer and the gap, a protractor against the lane line for the angle, a top photo for the panel side and the fronts.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The road, its lines and the crashed car are fixed. Each vehicle is one rigid body of boxes: its wheels do not turn, so it is lifted and carried rather than driven, and traffic is not simulated. The scorer sees only the vehicles, so one held still within 3 mm of the road counts as parked. The painted lines are 3 mm wide, wider than true scale, so the top camera shows them. The buffer and gap are this task's SOP (departments vary).
reset_notes: Stand the fire engine in lane 2 with its middle at x 25.55 cm, y +33.0 cm, heading downstream (front toward -y, pump panel toward the median), and the ambulance on the near shoulder with its middle at x 17.0 cm, y -37.0 cm, front toward +y (rear doors away from the car), both upright on their bases. The road, lines, arrows and crashed car are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
